headword: {森羅万象|しんらばんしょう}
gloss: all things in the universe; all of creation; everything

definitions.explanation: Everything that exists in the universe, all phenomena and entities without exception.

examples.japanese: {仏教|ぶっきょう}では{森羅万象|しんらばんしょう}は{無常|むじょう}であると{説|と}く。
examples.english: Buddhism teaches that all things in the universe are impermanent.

examples.japanese: {自然|しぜん}は{森羅万象|しんらばんしょう}の{源|みなもと}である。
examples.english: Nature is the source of all things in existence.

examples.japanese: {森羅万象|しんらばんしょう}に{命|いのち}が{宿|やど}ると{信|しん}じられていた。
examples.english: It was believed that life dwells in all things in the universe.

notes:
FOUR-CHARACTER IDIOM ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}):
{森羅|しんら} (dense, countless things) + {万象|ばんしょう} (myriad phenomena)

COMPONENTS:
- {森|しん}: forest, dense
- {羅|ら}: net, to spread out
- {万|ばん}: ten thousand, myriad
- {象|しょう}: phenomenon, form

ORIGIN:
Derived from Buddhist philosophy, particularly the concept that all things are interconnected and part of one universal whole.

USAGE:
Used in philosophical, religious, or literary contexts to refer to the totality of existence. Common in discussions of Buddhism, Shinto, or nature.

CULTURAL CONNECTION:
Relates to the Japanese concept of {万物|ばんぶつ} (all things) and the Shinto belief that spirits ({神|かみ}) inhabit all natural phenomena.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {万物|ばんぶつ}: all things
- {宇宙|うちゅう}: the universe
- {天地万物|てんちばんぶつ}: all things in heaven and earth
